html:
SMTO-GWT-0085 — A job on the Gateway lost contact with the Gateway

GUID: a0aa65f8-20e6-5624-8649-c7edcb0e0bae
Slug: gateway-worker-unavailable
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • Each job on the Gateway computer reports back to the main Gateway program. This job couldn't reach it. The job itself may still be running.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for this Gateway. This shows whether the main Gateway program is running and answering.
  2. Ask the person who manages the Gateway whether it was just restarted or updated, or is running many jobs at once. A job loses contact when the main program restarts or is too busy to accept it.
  3. Look at the Task in the conversation and check whether the job's result already exists before asking SMTO to run it again. The job may have kept running and finished its work even while it couldn't report back.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows as connected and the Task shows a clear final result for the job.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't delete the Gateway's saved data or start a second copy of the job while the first one's result is unknown.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway job worker could not establish or keep a valid local connection to its owning Gateway process (owner unavailable or not matching, connection capacity or deadline exhausted, readiness timeout, or full control queue).

What this means

  • Local worker attachment could not prove a live matching owner or child provenance, exhausted connection capacity or its deadline, failed readiness, or filled the pending control queue. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Local worker attachment could not prove a live matching owner or child provenance, exhausted connection capacity or its deadline, failed readiness, or filled the pending control queue.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect owner PID and creation time, worker ticket, attach/connection timing, control backlog and any retained terminal receipt.

How to fix it

  • Check that the Gateway process is running and healthy on that host (Check connection, Gateway log), and whether it was restarted or is overloaded with jobs. Inspect the job's retained status before reconnecting or relaunching; a lost worker connection does not prove the command stopped, so do not start a replacement until the original job is reconciled.
  • Check Gateway health, local worker capacity and owner diagnostics. Reconnect the worker only after checking retained job status.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The original worker and owner reconnect and reconcile the same job, or retained evidence settles its final state.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
